svg.text: Step 6 - reverse leakage. Rewire from the sweep rig.
The bank comes off, the die is driven BACKWARDS, and the meter reads ACROSS THE DIE. Healthy reads near 5 V; a shunt pulls it down.
top half + both top rails: leave empty
rail holes: first at col 3, then five, a one-hole gap, five, ...
die Dn: anode = pin 4n-2 red K = 4n-3 green K = 4n-1 blue K = 4n
REMOVE these six D2-D7 jumpers - that kills the bank
everything faded stays on the board, it is simply not used
the meter goes across the DIE, not across the resistor
PULL the six jumpers off UNO D2-D7. Bank is dead.
ADD the 100 k across the top half: F10 to F14.
MOVE F/M #1 to G14, out to the die CATHODE.
MOVE F/M #2 to GND rail col 28, out to the ANODE.
DMM on DC VOLTS, 20 V range. Not millivolts.
Red probe in J14, black in any GND rail hole.
Wait 5 seconds, then read the volts.
Low reading = a conducting path around the junction.
The 100 k and the die form a divider off the 5 V rail.
The die's own resistance sets the reading.
5 V reverse maximum. Never exceed it.
